holidays.name: International Day of the Tropics
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating the tropical regions of the world, home to about 40% of the global population and a huge share of its biodiversity. Think palm trees, coral reefs, rainforests, and a lot of sunshine.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2016, with the first observance in 2017, to highlight the unique challenges and opportunities of tropical countries.
holidays.funFact: The tropics are home to more than half of the world's known plant and animal species, even though they cover only about 40% of the planet's surface.

holidays.name: Camera Day
holidays.description: A day for snapping photos, dusting off old film cameras, and remembering that the camera in your pocket was once a bulky box requiring chemicals and patience.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created to celebrate photography and the people who capture life's moments, held annually on June 29.
holidays.funFact: The first photograph ever taken, around 1826 by Nicéphore Niépce, required an exposure time of several hours, possibly even days.

holidays.name: Almond Buttercrunch Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the sweet, crunchy, buttery toffee candy coated in chocolate and sprinkled with chopped almonds. Dentists remain neutral, but your sweet tooth will not.
holidays.origin: A food holiday created by candy lovers and snack enthusiasts, observed every June 29 as a tribute to this classic confection.
holidays.funFact: Almonds are technically not true nuts but the seeds of a fruit related to peaches, so almond buttercrunch is secretly a stone fruit candy.

holidays.name: Hug Holiday
holidays.description: A day to give a hug to anyone who needs one, whether it's friends, family, or a very reluctant coworker. Consent is encouraged and highly recommended.
holidays.origin: An informal, grassroots observance promoting the emotional benefits of human touch and affection, marked on June 29 in some holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Studies suggest that a hug lasting at least 20 seconds can trigger the release of oxytocin, often nicknamed the 'cuddle hormone.'

holidays.name: Rat Day
holidays.description: Don't scurry away! This day celebrates the surprisingly clever, social, and affectionate rat, often misunderstood and maligned despite making fantastic pets and being a scientific hero.
holidays.origin: An unofficial animal appreciation observance often listed on June 29 in quirky holiday calendars, aimed at improving the public image of rodents.
holidays.funFact: Rats are known to laugh when tickled, emitting ultrasonic chirps that humans can't hear without special equipment.
